Subject: Reliability probes & pricing delta — post-demo recap

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid questions. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can get a focused proof-of-concept (PoC) running quickly.

Summary from the demo (high level)
- Redwood key differentiators called out: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, auto KV/prefix caching, and explicit batching controls to reduce per-token cost.
- You asked for head-to-head reliability/behavior vs the hyperscaler, plus an apples-to-apples cost delta on a typical SpectraHealth workload.

Proposed quick probes (2–3 day cycle, can be extended):
1) Sustained QPS profile: 60 qps steady-state with 512-token sequences for 2 hours (measure latency P50/P95/P99, token cost).
2) Burst & rate-limit behavior: 500 concurrent short requests for 10 minutes to exercise burst throttles and any 429 behavior.
3) Failover ramp: simulate a region outage (route to fallback model variant) and measure failover convergence time and error budget consumption.

Owners / ask list
- SpectraHealth: provide sample payloads (anonymized), preferred test window, and acceptance criteria (latency targets, max allowed error spikes).
- Redwood: Ben will lead the failover & throttle probes; Markus will run throughput/load tests; I will coordinate procurement/SOW items.

Attachments included: poc-test-script-v1.md (detailed test steps), redwood-hyperscaler-slo-matrix.xlsx (initial SLO comparison), spectra_poc_mvp_requirements.pdf (your requirements we discussed).

Next immediate asks
- Samir / Alicia: can you confirm target latency thresholds (P95 < X ms) and whether you want cross-region failover during the PoC?
- Also flag any procurement constraints (PO timelines, legal redlines).

Suggested kickoff: Mon 22 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT (30–45 min) to align owners and test gates. I can send a calendar invite once we confirm.

Thanks — Lauren

Lauren — thanks for the write-up and the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side that will shape the PoC:

Targets we care about:
- Latency: P95 < 450 ms for 512-token sequences (end-to-end, including any pre/post-processing).
- Availability: we want data to show sustained availability >= 99.9% during the test windows and graceful degradation under stress.
- Cost: we need a modeled per-1M token delta vs our current hyperscaler baseline (their managed endpoint + accelerator).

Specific asks
- Can Redwood run the burst test against our real access pattern (spikes with short prompts + embeddings calls)? We'll provide a sanitized sample corpus.
- We also need to map rate-limit behavior to our client-side backoff strategy — if we see 429s, what's the retry recommendation?

Procurement note: procurement will likely ask for a 2-week pilot estimate (ballpark $) and an initial SOW/statement of work we can route to legal. Also we have a short SOC 2 questionnaire that Alicia will share — does Redwood have a contact to coordinate evidence for security controls?

Appreciate it — Samir

Samir — quick baseline numbers and suggested plan from Redwood's ops side (summary; details in attached SLO matrix):

SLO / SLA comparisons (initial)
- Redwood hosted SLA: 99.95% (monthly). That corresponds to ~21.6 minutes of allowed downtime per month.
- Typical hyperscaler managed inference endpoints we benchmark against: often published 99.9% SLA, but implementation varies and regional failover often requires explicit multi-region config (additional cost). That corresponds to ~43.8 minutes/month of downtime allowance.
- Rate-limits: Redwood's hosted plans have soft burst throttles and a predictable backoff header (Retry-After). Our default shared tier will impose stricter qps limits; for PoC we can allocate a dedicated capacity slice (burst headroom and fixed qps) to avoid noisy-neighbor 429s.

Observed failover behavior (summary)
- In our failover drills, model variant fallback + routing convergence typically completes within 20–90 seconds depending on KV cache warmup; initial error spike (5–30s) during cutover is typical if KV cache is cold. We can pre-warm KV state for SpectraHealth to minimize that window.

Suggested PoC schedule (compact)
- Day 0: legal/PO + SOW signed, credentials and sanitized payloads collected.
- Day 1: run sustained QPS test (Markus) and capture latency/cost.
- Day 2: run burst + failover probes (Ben leads), validate retry behavior and capture traces.

Deliverables
- PoC report with latency P50/P95/P99, error events timeline, failover convergence charts, and a modeled cost delta vs your hyperscaler baseline.

What we need from SpectraHealth
- Sanitized sample requests (anonymized), contact for SOC 2 evidence (Alicia?), and a preferred 48-hour test window.

Attaching the initial SLO matrix and the PoC test script we discussed. I'll own the failover run and provide timelines.

— Ben
